conventions.block: block l = decoder block l (0-based); output = hidden_states[l+1]
conventions.S: [p1, spec_end): first token of 'Task:' .. last user token
conventions.k: generated position k = absolute P+k-1 (token k is the input; predicts k+1)
conventions.crn: slot (task, template, k) -> u_stream(task, template, k), identical in every arm

c2f.ablation: mean-ablation of the o_proj-input slice of each head at generated positions (decode steps only), mean over the task's 100 NEUTRAL programs

u1b.note: (a) decode at M=20 is position independent, so CRN coupling across arms is exact; (b)/(c) teacher forcing must run at batch 1 for states to depend only on the prefix

deviations.what: FP8 W8A8-dynamic quantisation (E4M3, per-output-channel weight scales, per-token activation scales; lm_head/embeddings/norms bf16) of the pinned bf16 Qwen3-8B weights
deviations.why: the GPU is a 16 GB RTX 2000 Ada (plan: 20 GB A4500); bf16 weights need 16.4 GB. F2 named bitsandbytes 8-bit only because it assumed a GPU without FP8; no C compiler is available for Triton kernels
deviations.check: U7: T2 ban 2/20 Dijkstra (<= 6/20 required), twin 20/20 (>= 17/20 required) with exp8's prompts and uniform keys

deviations.what: batches of 20 rows (two 10-slot blocks of the same task and template, or one 20-slot block)
deviations.why: throughput; every batch in every arm has the same shape, so CRN coupling stays exact (U1, U2a, U2d)

deviations.what: N=50 arms without a natural batch partner get the slots k 10-19 as extra rows (SUB_plain on all tasks; ADD alpha 1 when ADD alpha 0.5 ran)
analysis code hash-committed at commit #2 (before any ban sample) instead of commit #1
deviations.why: time; the decision rules were committed verbatim at commit #1

deviations.what: U3 criterion: aligned teacher-forced vs sampling states differ by <= 15% (max) and the mean aligned difference is < 1/4 of the off-by-one difference
deviations.why: FP8 decode and prefill use different GEMM shapes, so the same state differs by a few % (aligned mean 5.2% vs 82% off by one); the test confirms the position convention

deviations.what: judge cap raised from USD 0.20 to 0.40
deviations.why: T2 ban programs often leave both mechanical labellers unresolved

deviations.what: clean twin states for the ADD/RAND/SUB_affine hooks are recomputed at sampling time from a clean prefill (identical prompt and engine) instead of being stored on disk
deviations.why: equivalent and cheaper; U2a shows alpha=0 reproduces the clean twin exactly

deviations.what: 0g uses 100 sequences per corpus (25 per exp12 group) and base outputs capped at 512 new tokens
deviations.why: time; the base model runs in a separate load

deviations.what: 5c H1 null uses 100 coordinate permutations (plan: 500) and figures are rendered with matplotlib directly
C2e permutation null: 500 within-template permutations for T1/T2, 200 for bench tasks and the archive-pooled secondary analysis; full refits incl. inner CV
deviations.why: time (bench tasks are secondary to T1/T2 for C2e)

deviations.what: displacement-targeted ADD (protocol clarification from the plan) and SUBTRACT run in the prompt prefill only; generation reads the edited KV cache with no decode-time hooks

teacher-forced states were first extracted in 20-row batches; under FP8 W8A8 a row's state then depends on its position in the batch (GEMM tiling): identical prefixes differed by 4-8% (relative L2). The C2e and 5a states were re-extracted at batch 1 as the plan specifies; the batch-20 C2e run is kept as a sensitivity analysis (results/c2e_batch20_sensitivity.json); the 5c states stay from 20-row batches (descriptive only)
deviations.why: found by the C2e determinism check; U1b quantifies it and shows decode at M=20 is row-position independent, so the CRN coupling of the behavioural arms is unaffected

deviations.what: exploratory additions outside the frozen rules: 12 extra random directions (seeds 9004-9015, same construction) at alpha 1 on T2, T1, T03; a C2e extension to generated positions 24-96 with a bag-of-tokens text control (results/c2e_extension.json)
deviations.why: the frozen C2e window (tokens 1-16) ends before the class-divergent text (T2 median first divergence = 29 tokens); 3 random controls give a coarse picture of the random-direction distribution

deviations.what: 0g: the first attempt stopped at an assertion (exp1 sample ids repeat across paraphrases; the corpus key now includes paraphrase_id) and produced no numbers; it was re-run after S8

drop_decisions: secondary C1 rows: forecasts committed (commit #2), event rows not scored (drop item 1)

predictions.P1: ADD at alpha 1 or 2 beats every random control on >= 2/3 of the gated tasks and lands on the named ban's modal survivor.
predictions.P2: SUB raises the banned share by >= 0.3.
predictions.P3: C2e: no position beats the text controls by 0.10. State and text curves rise together at the first divergent token; the expected T2 fork is the import line, tokens 3-5.
predictions.P4: C2f: T1 banned share rises >= 0.15 over random heads, T2 is unchanged.
predictions.P5: 0g: PASS by the frozen rule, with expected FR_zero about 0.98-0.995 for both models.
